Chyi Yu Promotional Portrait

Chyi Yu appears in a studio portrait wearing a bright red shawl draped over a dark, embellished top. Her hair is styled in a voluminous updo, and she offers a warm, gentle smile against a plain gray background. The image serves as the official artist photo on her Shazam page, where she is featured as a Mandopop singer with top songs, music videos, and curated playlists.

source.description:
Chyi Yu’s 1988 Album "有沒有這種說法"

Chyi Yu’s third Mandarin studio album, released in 1988, marked a bold departure from her previous folk-inspired image. The cover features a blue-hued portrait of the singer looking directly at the viewer, with the album title “有沒有這種說法” and her name in vertical yellow text.

Produced by her brother Chyi Chin under the newly formed Rainbow Music Studio, the album was arranged by 20-year-old Tu Hui-yuan, who combined MIDI soundscapes with a rock band setup. source.title: Evergreen like the olive tree: Veteran singer Chyi Yu to perform with SCO for Mother’s Day | The Straits Times
source.description:
Chyi Yu’s Mother’s Day Performance

Chyi Yu appears in a serene, high-key portrait, her dark hair softly tousled and her hands resting gracefully on a white surface. She wears a translucent, pale blouse and jade jewelry, her warm smile reflecting decades of musical experience. This image introduces her upcoming concerts with the Singapore Chinese Orchestra on May 10 and 11, 2024, celebrating Mother’s Day with a program that bridges folk-pop and Chinese classical music.

source.description:
Qi Yu’s Timeless Presence

Qi Yu, born in Taichung in 1957, has long been celebrated for her ethereal voice and influential role in Mandarin pop music. After studying anthropology at National Taiwan University and UCLA, she launched a career marked by classics such as “Olive Tree” and award-winning film themes. Her performance of “Huan Yan” on the 2019 season of “Singer” secured her a strong second-place finish, reaffirming her status as a “hall of fame” vocalist.
